thesis: Anthony Edwards transformed from promising prospect to franchise centerpiece, guiding the Timberwolves to back-to-back Western Conference Finals appearances and breaking Kevin Garnett's playoff scoring record in just five seasons.

facts.claim: Edwards led the 56–26 Timberwolves in the 2023–24 regular season, averaging 25.9 points and becoming the third-youngest player to score 6,000 career points.
In the 2024 playoffs, Edwards averaged 31 points and 8 rebounds per game while sweeping the Phoenix Suns in the first round, including 40 points in the final game.
At age 23, Edwards surpassed Kevin Garnett's franchise playoff scoring record of 1,049 points, accumulating 1,065 points in five seasons versus Garnett's 12 seasons.
Edwards reached back-to-back Western Conference Finals appearances in 2024 and 2025, ending a 20-year drought since the franchise's last conference finals trip in 2004.
The Timberwolves won 49 or more games in consecutive seasons for the first time in over two decades with Edwards as the unquestioned franchise cornerstone.
Edwards was drafted No. 1 overall in 2020, finished second in Rookie of the Year voting, and the franchise made first-round exits in 2022 and 2023 before his breakout 2023–24 season.
